::: notes
Welcome. We have two halves with a break between them, and one published claim to work on throughout. In the first half I introduce the vocabulary of reproduction, robustness and replication, and then the case study, an experiment in which just over a thousand emails asked housing authorities in the United States how to apply for public housing, and in which the replies to Hispanic names were less likely to greet the sender by name. We work out which question that claim answers, and you reproduce one of the five independent reanalyses of it, the one that I give you. In the second half you vary the analysis yourself, we place your choices among every justifiable analysis of these data, and we finish with the new experiment that tested the claim again. Everything runs in these slides, which run R inside your browser, so there is nothing to install.
:::
